Lessons.Title: The Size of Angles on a Clock
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will describe the size of an angle as a turn of one ray to the other.
In this lesson, you use an analog clock as a tool to describe the size of angles. You begin by using the clock to help describe how to draw a given angle, which involves describing the positions of the two hands of the clock. This work encourages you to relate the turning of the hands in a circular arc to the turning of rays of an angle around your shared endpoint.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Two Sets of Angles (10 minutes); Activity 1: Draw Angles Andre’s Way (15 minutes); Activity 2: Compare Angles on the Clock (20 minutes); Cool-down: Which Angle is Larger? By How Much? (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: At an exact hour, clock-hour marks are spaced by 30 degrees; the smaller angle is the relevant turn unless otherwise specified.

Edulytics authored guidance: Explain the clock-hand ray model: 12 to 3 makes a quarter turn of 90°. At exactly 5:00, the smaller angle between hands is 150°. At 6:00, hands point in opposite directions, giving a straight angle of 180°.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): At exactly 8:00, what is the smaller angle between the hands?
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
